at-the-fountain-sweet-smell-of-success: Sidney Falco's hungry, driving number from Sweet Smell of Success makes a strong audition choice for tenors and basses who want to show ambition and bite. This is a two-minute audition cut in D major, recorded with full production so the momentum never drops while you sell the story. Use it for a 32-bar slot or a self-tape where the panel needs to hear drive, diction and a confident top.
born-to-entertain-ruthless: "Born to Entertain" is Tina Denmark's ruthless bid for the spotlight, and it works best when you play the comedy completely straight. This full-song track in C major runs just under two minutes and is pitched for sopranos and altos. It's a good pick for young performers, cabaret sets and comedic auditions where you want a complete number with a clear button, rather than a 16-bar excerpt.
bundle-come-alive-tightrope-from-now-on-: Three Greatest Showman songs in one download: "Come Alive", "Tightrope" and "From Now On". These are note-bash tracks, so the melody is played clearly over the accompaniment to help you learn notes and entries fast. It's aimed at tenors and runs about three and a half minutes across the set. Handy for choirs, school productions and concert rehearsals where several singers need to learn the same material quickly.
bye-room-john-and-jen: "Bye Room" from Andrew Lippa's John & Jen is an intimate, conversational ballad that suits singers who can act through a lyric. This full-song track in G major runs about three minutes forty and is pitched for tenors and altos. Use it for showcases, recitals or longer audition slots where the panel wants to watch a full scene play out, not just a single emotional peak.
congratulations-professor-higgins-my-fai: A note-bash track of "Congratulations Professor Higgins" from My Fair Lady in F major, with the melody played clearly so you can lock in notes and rhythms. There are two versions: one for sopranos and altos and one for tenors and basses, so each part can rehearse at the right pitch. Best for ensemble learning, community and school productions, or anyone who needs to drill the part at home before rehearsals.
die-on-this-hill-sienna-spiro: Sienna Spiro's "Die On This Hill" gives contemporary singers a pop ballad with real emotional weight. This full-song piano track in A♭ major runs about three and a half minutes and suits sopranos and altos. It's a good fit for gigs, pop-rock auditions, song-cycle concerts and self-tapes where a stripped-back piano version lets your phrasing carry the song instead of a produced backing.
earth-sea-sky-lin-marsh: "Earth, Sea, Sky" by Lin Marsh is a full-song track in F major lasting about two and a half minutes. The piano part is recorded at a steady, supportive tempo, which makes it useful for school concerts, choir rehearsals and solo practice at home where singers need a reliable accompaniment. Voice type isn't listed for this track yet, so check the preview against your range before you buy.
for-better-or-worse-the-great-gatsby: From the Broadway musical The Great Gatsby, "For Better Or Worse" is a soaring ballad for sopranos and altos. This audition cut in B♭ major runs under two minutes, recorded in one expressive take so it breathes like a live pianist. It's a fresh, contemporary choice for auditions and self-tapes when you want something panels haven't heard a hundred times this season.
glitter-and-be-gay-candide: Cunegonde's coloratura showpiece from Bernstein's Candide is the classic test of agility, range and comic timing for sopranos. This audition cut runs about a minute and a half with full production, so the orchestral sparkle stays behind you while you land the runs and top notes. Use it for classical-leaning musical theatre auditions, opera-crossover calls and competitions that want a genuine vocal showpiece.
how-it-ends-big-fish: Edward Bloom's closing song from Andrew Lippa's Big Fish is a warm, reflective ballad that rewards honest storytelling. This audition cut for tenors in D major runs just under two minutes and is recorded with a polished, expressive feel. It's a good choice when you need a legit-leaning contemporary ballad that shows warmth and maturity, for auditions, self-tapes or a showcase.
i-like-christmas-for-the-food-katie-thom: Katie Thompson's "I Like Christmas for the Food" is a full-song track in C major, about three and a half minutes long and pitched for tenors and basses. It's made for the festive season: Christmas concerts, carol nights, cabaret sets and end-of-year showcases where you want something lighter and less expected than the usual carols. The full production keeps the energy up from start to finish.
i-need-more-writing-kevin-taylor: "I Need More" comes in two versions: a two-and-a-half-minute audition cut and a full four-and-a-half-minute performance track, both in G major for sopranos and altos. Pick the cut for audition rooms and self-tapes where time is short, or the full song for concerts and showcases where you can build the whole arc. The polished recording keeps the accompaniment expressive without getting in your way.
listen-to-the-rain-lin-marsh: Lin Marsh's "Listen to the Rain" is a short full-song track in C major, running about eighty seconds. Its length makes it an easy fit for concert programmes, assemblies, lessons and practice where a complete song needs to sit alongside other pieces. The steady piano part supports singers who are still building confidence. Voice type isn't listed yet, so check the preview against your range first.
love-on-the-rocks-neil-diamond: Neil Diamond's "Love on the Rocks" is a slow-burning pop ballad, recorded here as a full-song piano track in F major for altos. At a little over four minutes it gives you room to build from a restrained opening to a big finish. It's ideal for cabaret, weddings, gigs and pop auditions where a piano-only arrangement shows off the voice.
love-revolution-cy-coleman: "Love Revolution" by Cy Coleman is recorded here as an audition cut in F major for altos. Coleman's writing rewards singers with rhythmic confidence and a bit of swagger, so this cut suits auditions and self-tapes for jazz-inflected or classic Broadway shows. The polished recording keeps the groove steady so you can focus on style and storytelling rather than counting bars.
make-a-wish-kimberly-akimbo: Kimberly's wistful song from the Tony-winning Kimberly Akimbo, recorded as a full-song track in B♭ major for sopranos and altos. At just over five minutes, it's the whole number, so you can build the character's hope and humour across the complete arc. Use it for recitals, showcases and longer audition slots, or for learning the song properly before you choose your own cut.
make-them-hear-you-ragtime: Coalhouse Walker's anthem from Ragtime is one of the great audition songs for tenors and basses who can carry a big, sustained line. This audition cut in E♭ major runs just under two minutes and is recorded with full production for the swell the song demands. Choose it when a panel needs to hear power, conviction and vocal stamina in a short slot.
naughty-matilda-jr: Matilda's defiant anthem from Tim Minchin's Matilda JR. is recorded here as a full-song track in F major, about eighty seconds long. It's pitched for young performers working on the junior edition, so it naturally suits school and youth-theatre auditions, rehearsals and at-home practice. The polished accompaniment keeps the tempo clear, which really helps with the song's tricky patter and rhythms.
people-will-say-were-in-love-oklahoma: Laurey and Curly's teasing duet from Rodgers and Hammerstein's Oklahoma!, recorded as an audition cut in A major for sopranos. It's a go-to for golden-age auditions where the panel wants a clean legit sound, clear diction and a light, playful touch of character. The polished recording keeps the tempo buoyant and supportive, so the long phrases sit easily in the voice.
she-loves-me: Georg's joyful title song from Bock and Harnick's She Loves Me, recorded as a short audition cut of just over a minute. Two versions are available: one in E♭ major and a full-production version in A♭ major for tenors and basses. It's ideal for a 16-bar slot where you want to show charm, comic timing and a secure top in very little time.
silver-moon-lin-marsh: "Silver Moon" by Lin Marsh is a gentle full-song track in G major, running about three and a half minutes. The accompaniment gives singers space to shape long phrases, which makes it good for lyrical concert items, choir preparation and solo practice at home. Voice type hasn't been listed for this recording yet, so play the preview first to check the key suits you.
stars-lin-marsh: Lin Marsh's "Stars" is a full-song piano track in A major, about two minutes long. The clear, even accompaniment makes it a dependable choice for school concerts, choir rehearsals and singers practising a complete song on their own. Voice type isn't listed for this track yet, so check the preview against your range, or order a custom recording in a key that suits you better.
streets-of-dublin-a-man-of-no-importance: Robbie's high-spirited love letter to his city, from Flaherty and Ahrens' A Man of No Importance. This audition cut for tenors in E major runs about two and a half minutes, with full production to drive the song's lilting, celebratory energy. Choose it when you want to show warmth, an easy top and storytelling in a contemporary legit style that stands out from the usual picks.
summer-lin-marsh: "Summer" by Lin Marsh is a full-song track in D major that runs about three and a half minutes. The bright accompaniment suits concerts, end-of-term performances and practice sessions where singers want a complete song to work through from start to finish. Voice type isn't listed for this recording yet, so check the preview first, or order a custom track in your own key.
taylor-the-latte-boy-marcy-heisler-and-z: Goldrich and Heisler's comic ode to a coffee-shop crush is a long-standing audition favourite for sopranos and altos with great comic timing. This audition cut in B♭ major runs about two minutes and has full production to support the song's quick shifts of mood. Use it for comedic audition slots, cabaret and showcases where you want to show character and personality.
through-the-mountain-floyd-collins: "Through the Mountain" is from Adam Guettel's Floyd Collins, one of the most demanding scores in contemporary musical theatre. This full-song track in C major runs about four minutes and is pitched for sopranos. The polished recording handles Guettel's shifting harmonies, so you can concentrate on line and colour. It's best suited to recitals, showcases and learning the full piece in depth.
tonight-at-eight-she-loves-me: Georg's nervous patter song from She Loves Me, recorded as a tight 52-second audition cut in D major for tenors and basses. It's built for a 16-bar slot where you want to show diction, rhythmic precision and comic nerves without rushing. The polished accompaniment keeps a clear pulse under the fast text, which makes it good for practising the patter at speed before the room.
underground-cody-fry: Cody Fry's "Underground" is a contemporary pick for tenors and basses who want something outside the standard musical theatre book. This one-minute audition cut in F major has full production, so the groove stays tight while you sell the style. It works well for pop-rock auditions, contemporary self-tapes and showcases where the panel wants to hear your own voice rather than a Broadway imitation.
will-he-like-me-she-loves-me: Amalia's tender, anxious ballad from She Loves Me is a classic legit audition choice for sopranos. There are two audition-cut versions in G major, about a minute and a half long: a polished take and a full-production take, so you can choose the feel that suits your voice. Use it to show a warm soprano line, clear storytelling and vulnerability in a short slot.
with-a-little-bit-of-luck-my-fair-lady: Alfred P. Doolittle's cheeky music-hall number from My Fair Lady, recorded as a note-bash track in C major with the melody played clearly. There are two versions: a full-length one for sopranos and altos and a short one for tenors and basses. Use them to learn notes and rhythms for ensemble or chorus parts, or to drill the tune before rehearsals start.
